season_storylines: Seattle won Super Bowl LX but Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III left for Kansas City on a 3-year $45M deal, diluting his TD equity in a controlled Chiefs committee while opening a valuable Seahawks goal-line role for Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet.

Mike McDaniel is now the Chargers' offensive coordinator, making Justin Herbert a premium 6-pt-passing-TD buy and setting up Omarion Hampton (back from his rookie ankle fracture) for elite early-down volume plus 21%-of-early-down-pass-attempts RB usage.

Atlanta signed Tua Tagovailoa to a one-year deal to battle Michael Penix Jr., who is still not cleared from his Week 11 2025 ACL tear, and new HC Kevin Stefanski's bottom-5 neutral pass rate history funnels TD equity to Bijan Robinson while capping Falcons pass-catchers.

Season-ending camp injuries are stacking up: 49ers WR Ricky Pearsall (knee) is out for 2026, consolidating San Francisco targets on George Kittle and the veteran receivers, while Carolina lost edge Nic Scourton (ACL) and WR Chris Brazzell and the Saints lost DT Bryan Bresee.

Contract standoffs are live fantasy risk: Jahmyr Gibbs wants a new Lions deal while nursing a back issue Dan Campbell downplays, and Baker Mayfield is in a public contract dispute with Tampa Bay while Vita Vea requests a trade.

The DJ Moore trade from Chicago to Buffalo vacates a 16% target share for second-year Luther Burden III under Ben Johnson, while Moore himself lands in a slow-paced Bills committee coming off three straight years of efficiency decline (YPRR 2.31 to 1.24).

Matthew Stafford, now 38, is priced at QB9 after leading the NFL with 4707 yards and a career-high 46 TDs at age 37; that TD rate is a regression candidate even in 6-pt-passing-TD formats, so pay for the profile, not last year's line.

Aaron Rodgers declared 2026 his final season with zero debate, reuniting with new Steelers HC Mike McCarthy, and camp reports say the Rodgers-to-DK Metcalf connection is surging, stabilizing Metcalf's downfield TD-driven value.

Betting markets frame the extremes: Baltimore's 11.5 win total with the 6th-easiest schedule is the league's highest, Cincinnati is a heavy -140 over 9.5 with the 2nd-easiest schedule (favored in 15 of 17), and Miami and Arizona sit at 4.5, gutting TD-dependent assets there.

The coaching carousel rewired half the league: Kevin Stefanski (ATL), Todd Monken (CLE), Jesse Minter (BAL), Mike LaFleur (ARI), Robert Saleh with OC Brian Daboll (TEN), Mike McCarthy (PIT), Jeff Hafley with OC Bobby Slowik (MIA), and John Harbaugh with OC Matt Nagy (NYG) all reset run/pass identities fantasy prices have not fully caught up to.

teams.outlook: New HC Mike LaFleur brings McVay concepts but OC Nathaniel Hackett, a Brissett/Beck QB mess, and the league's lowest implied total (4.5 wins) mean only volume plays work here: No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love's projected ~289 touches and Trey McBride travel, while Marvin Harrison Jr. slides into the vacated outside X role as a talent-over-situation bet.

Kevin Stefanski's run-first, RB/TE-friendly scheme plus an unsettled Tua-vs-Penix QB battle (Penix not cleared from ACL) makes Bijan Robinson a TD-equity monster and caps every Falcons pass-catcher's weekly ceiling.

First-time HC Jesse Minter and first-time play-caller Declan Doyle inherit Lamar Jackson with a 24th-ranked OL that lost Tyler Linderbaum, so the 11.5-win market total and 6th-easiest schedule keep Lamar a top rushing-QB buy but downgrade the aging Mark Andrews pass-catching core; Tyreek Hill was added to the WR room (verify).

Buffalo stays bottom-5 in neutral pace with a WR-by-committee approach, so newly acquired DJ Moore (age 29, three straight years of YPRR decline) is a name-brand trap while Josh Allen's rushing plus 6-pt passing TDs keeps him the format's premier QB.

Rico Dowdle's departure leaves an inefficient Chuba Hubbard (3.8 YPC) versus a finally-cleared Jonathon Brooks for goal-line work, and the 3rd-hardest schedule plus Bryce Young's low pass volume caps Tetairoa McMillan in a non-PPR format that punishes his target-compiler profile.

Year 2 of Ben Johnson with Caleb Williams and DJ Moore's traded-away 16% target share makes Luther Burden III (2.92 rookie YPRR) the priority buy, with Colston Loveland's late-season 23% target share next in line and Rome Odunze carrying foot-injury risk (verify).

Joe Burrow is back, the defense added Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe after ranking last in TDs allowed, and Cincinnati is favored in 15 of 17 games with the 2nd-easiest schedule, so Bengals skill players carry elite team-total-driven TD equity all season.

New HC Todd Monken's Ravens-style scheme has always featured lead backs, making Quinshon Judkins the clearest coaching-change winner, while Harold Fannin Jr.'s rookie 21% target share now competes with drafted WRs KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston plus his own soft-tissue flags.

Javonte Williams smashed value last year (RB11) but was dead last in YPRR among 25-plus-target RBs with Jaydon Blue lurking for carries, and George Pickens' target gravity makes CeeDee Lamb's WR6 price rich for a format that ignores his catch volume.

Sean Payton traded the 30th pick for Jaylen Waddle, who has never hit 100 targets in a season, so the projected ~122-target WR1 role is scheme-dependent hope, and Bo Nix's modest passing efficiency keeps this a spread-it-around offense despite a 9.5-win market.

David Montgomery was traded to Houston, pointing Jahmyr Gibbs toward a monster non-PPR workload if his contract standoff and back tightness (Campbell says minor) resolve, while Sam LaPorta races a 10-month back-surgery rehab to be ready Week 1 with Jameson Williams the proven spike-week beneficiary.

Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks are gone, finally condensing routes for the extended Christian Watson (17.5 FPG above 75% route share), whose deep-ball TD profile fits this scoring far better than slot-bound Jayden Reed, with Matthew Golden's Year 2 a cheap swing.

C.J. Stroud gets a rebuilt rhythm game via traded-for David Montgomery, but Montgomery's age-29, 11-opportunities-per-game 2025 profile is a classic dead-zone fade, and Christian Kirk's exit plus Tank Dell's rehab make Jayden Higgins the red-zone-sized riser next to injury-prone Nico Collins.

Daniel Jones returns off his top-10 season but Michael Pittman's vacated ~21% target share has no obvious WR heir (Alec Pierce is coming off ankle surgery, Josh Downs has never played 2-WR sets), funneling Tyler Warren (21.2% rookie target share) toward a true every-down TE role.

Travis Etienne's departure to New Orleans hands the backfield to Bhayshul Tuten (97th-percentile breakaway rate, 7 TDs on 93 rookie touches) with Chris Rodriguez Jr. limited by a foot issue, a clean path to high-end RB2 value built on yardage and TDs.

Patrick Mahomes is back on the practice field and the Chiefs paid Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III $45M, but KC's historically controlled backfield rotation and Rashee Rice's uncertain role at a rich ADP (~28) make Chiefs skill players priced above their likely TD distribution.

New play-caller Klint Kubiak imports the Super Bowl-winning Seattle scheme with heavy 12 personnel, boosting Brock Bowers' route rate and giving Year 2 Ashton Jeanty real infrastructure behind boot-action, while added deep threat Rashid Shaheed brings return-game yardage this league actually pays for.

Mike McDaniel's arrival as OC is the offseason's biggest scheme win: Justin Herbert becomes a 6-pt-TD premium play, Omarion Hampton profiles for Achane-style RB1 usage, Ladd McConkey owns McDaniel's middle-of-field sweet spot, and David Njoku/Charlie Kolar chase a historically 20%-plus TE target share.

The Rams added Trent McDuffie from KC and carry a 10.5-win total, but 38-year-old Matthew Stafford at a QB9 price after a 46-TD career year is the definition of paying the top of the range; his receivers keep volume, just expect fewer scores to split.

A full teardown — new HC Jeff Hafley, OC Bobby Slowik, Malik Willis at QB, and Tua/Hill/Waddle all gone — plus a league-low 4.5 win total collapses the TD environment, making De'Von Achane a talent-trapped fade and everything else a desperation dart.

The backfield is the swing: veteran Aaron Jones faces a real challenge from the more efficient Jordan Mason for early-down and goal-line work, and until that settles neither is trustworthy for the TD-driven touches this format rewards (verify QB timeline).

The market is a believer at 9.5 wins with juiced over odds (-140) behind Drake Maye's ascent; his rushing gives him a stable 6-pt-TD floor, though the ADP now assumes the leap rather than discounting it.

Tyler Shough closed his rookie year with six straight 17-plus-point games and a 22.2% goal-line carry rate, and adding Travis Etienne and first-rounder Jordyn Tyson raises the ceiling, though Alvin Kamara still skims receiving/red-zone work and Chris Olave carries a reported blood-clot concern (verify).

John Harbaugh and OC Matt Nagy install a run-leaning, low-risk identity, so Malik Nabers returning to practice off his ACL (with a spring follow-up procedure) is a talent bet against both health and scheme, and no Giants pass-catcher should be priced for volume.

Geno Smith has been red-hot in Aaron Glenn's camp, repeatedly hitting Garrett Wilson for red-zone TDs, but a 5.5-win market total says the offense's scoring environment is thin — Breece Hall's TD share is the safest Jets asset in this format.

New OC Sean Mannion adds motion and vertical concepts for Jalen Hurts, positioning DeVonta Smith as the primary beneficiary and rookie Makai Lemon as the depth riser, while Hurts' rushing/goal-line TD monopoly remains the format's most stable cheat code.

Mike McCarthy's fantasy-friendly offense hosts Aaron Rodgers' declared farewell tour, with the DK Metcalf connection visibly clicking in camp and Rico Dowdle added to pair with Jaylen Warren — a sneaky TD-efficient ecosystem at an 8.5-win price, with Drew Allar developing behind.

The defending champs lost both OC Klint Kubiak and Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III, so the vacated lead-back TD role between explosive Jadarian Price (6.0 college YPC) and Zach Charbonnet is one of camp's most valuable unanswered questions at a 10.5-win team total.

Ricky Pearsall's season-ending knee injury and rookie RB Jordan James' rib fracture consolidate Kyle Shanahan's offense around Brock Purdy, George Kittle, and a Christian McCaffrey coming off a ~450-touch age-29 season — CMC's cliff risk is real even as his short-term volume stays elite; newly added Mike Evans is an age-33 scheme-fit question (verify).

Baker Mayfield's contract standoff and Vita Vea's trade request cloud camp, but Mike Evans' departure clears a genuine alpha runway for Emeka Egbuka, Kenny Gainwell inherits the passing-down role that produced 13.3 touches/game late last year, and Bucky Irving's ADP (~57) leans on weekly stability a brutal early schedule may not allow.

Robert Saleh brought Brian Daboll to call plays, a proven QB-elevator for Cam Ward's Year 2, and top rookie WR Carnell Tate's pro-ready route running gives Tennessee its first true go-to target with Chig Okonkwo's role expanding — a cheap stack at a 6.5-win price.

The market prices Washington at just 7.5 wins, but Jayden Daniels' rushing keeps his 6-pt-TD ceiling weekly-elite regardless of team environment; treat the supporting cast as matchup-based rather than every-week anchors (verify camp roles).

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Mike McDaniel's Chargers scheme gives RBs 21%-plus of early-down pass attempts and he flashed RB1 weeks (24.9 pts Week 3) before the rookie ankle fracture; healthy volume plus TD equity is exactly what non-PPR pays.

breakout_watch.name: Jeremiyah Love
breakout_watch.why: No. 3 overall pick projected for ~289 touches with elite speed and three-down ability; the last nine top-12 drafted RBs all finished top-12 as rookies, and raw yardage/TD volume beats his bad-team environment in this format.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Inherits Jacksonville's lead role from the departed Travis Etienne with a 97th-percentile breakaway rate and 7 TDs on just 93 rookie touches, while Chris Rodriguez Jr.'s foot issue clears his goal-line path.

breakout_watch.name: Luther Burden III
breakout_watch.why: DJ Moore's trade vacates a 16% target share in Ben Johnson's offense and Burden's 2.92 rookie YPRR ranked with elite prospects; downfield, YAC-heavy profile earns yardage points, not empty catches.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: Mike Evans' departure hands him the alpha X role with Baker Mayfield's aggressive downfield style; four 20-plus-point rookie games show the TD/yardage spike weeks this scoring rewards.

breakout_watch.name: Jayden Higgins
breakout_watch.why: Christian Kirk gone, Tank Dell rehabbing, and Nico Collins injury-prone; Higgins matched Collins' 6 TDs as a rookie and his red-zone size makes him a TD-equity riser rather than a slot compiler.

breakout_watch.name: Tyler Warren
breakout_watch.why: Posted a 21.2% target share as a rookie and Michael Pittman's vacated 21% share has no obvious WR heir with Alec Pierce coming off ankle surgery — every-down TE volume with red-zone usage.

breakout_watch.name: Tyler Shough
breakout_watch.why: Closed 2025 with six straight 17-plus-point games, ranked second in goal-line carry percentage (22.2%), and added Travis Etienne plus first-round WR Jordyn Tyson; rushing TDs plus 6-pt passing TDs stack his ceiling.

breakout_watch.name: Justin Herbert
breakout_watch.why: Mike McDaniel's efficient middle-of-field scheme should spike TD rate while suppressing INTs — the exact profile 6-pt-TD, -2-INT scoring pays a premium for, still priced as a sleeper.

breakout_watch.name: Cam Ward
breakout_watch.why: Brian Daboll's arrival as Titans play-caller (the coach behind Daniel Jones' top-10 season) plus pro-ready rookie target Carnell Tate gives Ward a real Year 2 TD-volume leap at a near-free price.

breakout_watch.name: Quinshon Judkins
breakout_watch.why: New HC Todd Monken has always funneled feature-back volume (Chubb, Henry lineage), making Judkins the clearest coaching-change winner for goal-line and early-down work in Cleveland.

breakout_watch.name: Jadarian Price
breakout_watch.why: The Super Bowl champs must replace Kenneth Walker III's lead role; Price's 6.0 college YPC and 13 scrimmage TDs on limited volume fit a high-scoring offense, though Zach Charbonnet caps the floor.

breakout_watch.name: Brock Bowers
breakout_watch.why: Klint Kubiak's 12-personnel-heavy, boot-action Seattle scheme drove huge TE route rates and lands in Vegas; Bowers gets the explosive intermediate throws that produce yardage points.

breakout_watch.name: Rashid Shaheed
breakout_watch.why: Signed with the Raiders as the field-stretcher in Kubiak's play-action scheme, and his punt/kick return work adds the return-yardage points (roughly 2.5-3 ppg) this league uniquely pays.

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: Age-30 season directly off a ~450-touch year with a career-low 3.8 YPC; the historical post-workload cliff is severe and his receiving cushion is worthless in zero-PPR scoring.

fade_watch.name: Matthew Stafford
fade_watch.why: Priced at QB9 at age 38 after a career-high 46-TD outlier; TD regression plus interception risk at -2 apiece makes the profile all downside from this price.

fade_watch.name: Kenneth Walker III
fade_watch.why: Kansas City's controlled committee has not supported a bell-cow, so the Super Bowl MVP's $45M name-brand price outruns his likely TD and carry share.

fade_watch.name: David Montgomery
fade_watch.why: Age-29, Year-8 back who fell to 11 opportunities per game in 2025; classic dead-zone profile in Houston with the trade cost inflating his perceived role.

fade_watch.name: DJ Moore
fade_watch.why: Three straight years of YPRR decline (2.31 to 1.24) into Buffalo's slow-paced WR-by-committee; a catch-volume compiler aging into a format that only pays yards and TDs.

fade_watch.name: Rashee Rice
fade_watch.why: Top-30 ADP despite unresolved role uncertainty, and his short-area, catch-heavy usage is exactly the production zero-PPR scoring discounts.

fade_watch.name: Malik Nabers
fade_watch.why: Back at practice but coming off an ACL tear with a spring follow-up procedure, learning a run-leaning Harbaugh/Nagy offense; elite target volume matters less here than health and TD access, and both are shaky.

fade_watch.name: De'Von Achane
fade_watch.why: Miami's 4.5-win teardown with Malik Willis at QB guts the TD environment and defenses will load the box; speed-efficiency profiles crater fastest in bad offenses.

fade_watch.name: Javonte Williams
fade_watch.why: Last season's RB11 finish came with dead-last YPRR among 25-plus-target backs, and Jaydon Blue lurks for passing-down and change-of-pace carries at a round-3/4 price that assumes a repeat.

fade_watch.name: Chuba Hubbard
fade_watch.why: 3.8 YPC with poor rushing-yards-over-expectation, a finally-healthy Jonathon Brooks cleared behind him, and the third-hardest schedule on a team that ranked 24th in red-zone TD rate.

uncertainty_note: Preseason games have not been played yet, so nothing is snap-count-proven: Atlanta's Tua-vs-Penix battle (Penix uncleared from ACL), the Gibbs and Mayfield contract standoffs, Sam LaPorta's and Malik Nabers' Week 1 readiness, the Seattle (Price/Charbonnet) and Carolina (Hubbard/Brooks) backfield splits, Rome Odunze's foot status, and several relocation reports from aggregated sources (Tyreek Hill to BAL, Mike Evans to SF, Derrick Henry's landing spot) remain unsettled or only partially verified — re-check all of these after the first preseason week.
